requirements.title: Sequential access accesses records in order
requirements.definition: Sequential access is a method of accessing records of an external record file in order.

pending.sequential-access-records-in-order: Write two known sequential records with distinct nondefault values and read them back with variables initialized to different sentinels; expect the same order.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

requirements.title: Sequential record order follows write order or direct record-number order
requirements.definition: For sequential access, record order is write order when direct access is not allowed for the file; if direct access is also allowed, sequential order is the direct record-number order starting with record number 1.

pending.sequential-order-written-order-without-d: For a controlled sequential-only file if available, write records A then B and read A then B; if support cannot be established, leave unexecuted rather than assume method set.
pending.sequential-order-direct-record-number-or: Only under a processor profile that allows both methods, write direct records with known numbers and read sequentially; assert record-number order, not physical layout.

requirements.title: Unwritten records shall not be read by sequential access
requirements.definition: A record that has not been written since the file was created shall not be read.

requirements.title: Sequential files normally end with an endfile record after non-output reference
requirements.definition: Unless the previous reference to the file was an output statement, the last record, if any, of a sequential file shall be an endfile record.

pending.sequential-last-record-endfile-unless-pr: Plan uses a controlled sequential file after input/positioning reference and reads to the named endfile condition; no portable oracle exists for inspecting an implementation endfile record directly.

review_rationale: Source registration for Clause 12 (batch145), the clause's first packet. Every base and fine unit classified and hash-verified against the pinned J3/24-007 census by an independent fresh-context reviewer who read the original pages 242-246 and confirmed 12.3.3.4 ends before 12.3.4.1. Mixed obligation/latitude units were swept in both directions and all splits recorded; no unit left unresolved; no numbered R/C rule in scope; no requirement based on a NOTE; no no-portable-oracle claim found to be over-suppression and no pending plan found vacuous. Source accounting only: no fixture, compiler invocation or execution credit.
